title: Phishing-Induced Security Breach
briefing: Multiple employees report suspicious emails requesting credential verification through a link to an external website. The security team must determine whether the campaign has already resulted in account compromise and how to respond.

injects.title: More Reports Surface
injects.message: Several additional employees report receiving the same email, suggesting the campaign may be larger than initially believed.

injects.title: Suspicious Login Activity
injects.message: Identity monitoring tools detect login attempts using credentials associated with users who reported the phishing email.

injects.title: Executive Concern
injects.message: Executives request confirmation on whether employee accounts may already be compromised.

injects.title: Customer Impact Question
injects.message: Customer-facing teams ask whether compromised employee accounts could expose sensitive data.

step_1.situation: Multiple users report a suspicious email that asks them to verify account credentials using an external link.

if_correct.consequence: The security team recognizes the phishing indicators and begins investigating the campaign.

if_incorrect.consequence: The email is initially dismissed as harmless, allowing the campaign to continue.

step_2.situation: Security teams review the email content and infrastructure used by the phishing campaign.

if_correct.consequence: Key phishing indicators are identified, helping confirm that the campaign is malicious.

if_incorrect.consequence: Failure to recognize key indicators delays the response.

step_3.situation: Security considers whether to restrict access to the phishing domain and block related network traffic.

if_correct.consequence: Blocking malicious infrastructure reduces the campaign’s effectiveness.

if_incorrect.consequence: Incomplete blocking allows additional employees to access the phishing site.

step_4.situation: The team evaluates whether stronger authentication controls could reduce the impact of stolen credentials.

if_correct.consequence: Additional authentication protections help prevent attackers from accessing compromised accounts.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak authentication protections increase the risk of credential abuse.

step_5.situation: Security teams prepare internal communications to warn employees about the phishing campaign.

if_correct.consequence: Timely warnings help employees avoid the phishing attempt and report suspicious messages.

if_incorrect.consequence: Delayed communication increases the chance that more employees fall for the phishing email.
